neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x4. Anxious but cooperative. Normal cognition.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II-XII intact. No ptosis. No diplopia. Normal facial strength.
neurological_exam.motor: Left arm: shoulder abductors 3/5, wrist extensors 3/5, hand intrinsics 3+/5. Right arm: shoulder abductors 4/5, wrist extensors 4/5. Bilateral lower extremities: hip flexors 3+/5 bilaterally, knee extensors 4/5, dorsiflexion 3/5 bilateral. Plantar flexion 4/5.
neurological_exam.sensory: Hyperalgesia and allodynia (pinprick and light touch) in bilateral extremities. Vibration markedly reduced at great toes (0 seconds — absent). Proprioception absent at toes and ankles bilaterally. Temperature sensation absent bilateral feet.

neurological_exam.coordination: Pseudoathetosis of outstretched hands bilaterally. Heel-shin impaired. Romberg positive (falls in 3 seconds).
neurological_exam.gait: Requires walker. Ataxic, wide-based. Bilateral steppage. Sensory ataxia with pseudoathetosis — suggests DRG involvement.
neurological_exam.special_tests: Livedo reticularis on forearms and legs bilaterally (visible). Pseudoathetosis present. No Babinski. No skin thickening. No rash.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive painful neuropathy with recent severe exacerbation following pregnancy
patient.history_present_illness: Sophie Tremblay is a 38-year-old registered dietitian presenting 6 weeks postpartum with a severe exacerbation of peripheral neuropathy that began during her pregnancy. She had a 2-year history of slowly progressive bilateral foot burning and tingling prior to pregnancy, attributed by a prior neurologist to 'idiopathic small fiber neuropathy.' She underwent normal NCS x2 and had skin biopsy confirming moderately reduced IENFD (4.8 fibers/mm) 18 months ago. During her third trimester, her neuropathy worsened dramatically with pain reaching 9/10, and she developed progressive weakness that made walking independently difficult. Six weeks postpartum, she is unable to walk without a walker, has hand weakness (particularly left), and has severe neuropathic pain with allodynia in all four extremities. She notes her prior symptoms were 'burning small fiber' in nature, but her current weakness seems different and more severe. She reports transient patches of skin reddening and mottling on her arms and legs. She breastfed for 3 weeks but stopped due to medication requirements. She had an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. She is a dietitian and has been reviewing her own diet — she has been vegan for 8 years but takes B12 supplements. She asks about potential toxic exposures. She does not drink alcohol and takes no medications other than prenatal vitamins. Prior neurologist's note says 'idiopathic SFN, monitor.'

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL (L), Platelets 88 K/uL (L), Peripheral smear Schistocytes 3+ (H), LDH 1,840 U/L (H), Haptoglobin <8 mg/dL (L), Total bilirubin 4.2 mg/dL (H), Direct bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL (H), Creatinine 2.8 mg/dL (H), eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73m² (L), ADAMTS13 activity 8% (L), ADAMTS13 inhibitor POSITIVE — 2.4 Bethesda units (H).

specialized_test.impression: ABNORMAL NCS/EMG — severe acute axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Motor and sensory nerve amplitudes markedly reduced or absent in all tested nerves bilaterally. Conduction velocities relatively preserved where measurable, consistent with amplitude-predominant axonal pattern. EMG: widespread active denervation (fibrillation potentials, positive sharp waves) in distal and proximal lower and upper extremity muscles bilaterally. Reduced or absent sensory nerve action potentials. Findings indicate severe acute axonal polyneuropathy superimposed on prior reduced IENFD findings

output.impression: TPE initiated within 12 hours of TTP diagnosis. Daily TPE x 10 sessions (1 plasma volume each, with FFP replacement). Caplacizumab 10 mg IV loading dose then 10 mg SQ daily added (anti-vWF nanobody, prevents platelet microvascular thrombosis). Rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly x4 scheduled (eliminates ADAMTS13 inhibitor-producing B cells). Response monitoring: ADAMTS13 activity, platelets, LDH, schistocyte count daily.

Hereditary vs Immune TTP Differentiation.value: No pathogenic variant detected — ADAMTS13 gene normal

Hereditary vs Immune TTP Differentiation.test: ADAMTS13 activity during remission (8 weeks post-TPE)

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: ADAMTS13 activity during remission (8 weeks post-TPE) 62% (L, ref >67%). ADAMTS13 gene sequencing shows no pathogenic variant; ADAMTS13 inhibitor negative during remission.

output.impression: Repeat skin biopsy 4 months post-TPE: Distal leg IENFD 3.4 fibers/mm (reference >6.8 fibers/mm) — still below normal but improved from 1.8 fibers/mm during acute phase (measured on admission). Proximal thigh IENFD 6.2 fibers/mm (reference >8.4 fibers/mm) — moderately reduced but improved from near-absent levels. Small fiber re-innervation occurring.

Repeat NCS/EMG 4 months post-TPE: Improving. Sural SNAP now present bilaterally (right 4.2 uV, left 3.8 uV — previously absent). Median motor amplitude improving bilaterally. EMG: reduced fibrillations in previously denervated muscles. Nascent MUPs (early reinnervation units) appearing in tibialis anterior. Pattern consistent with active reinnervation following recovery from acute TTP neuropathy.

output.query: TTP pregnancy relapse ADAMTS13 peripartum management

results.citation: Scully M et al. (2014) Pregnancy and TTP: ADAMTS13 activity monitoring. Blood 123:1-7.
results.summary: TTP has 17-25% relapse rate with subsequent pregnancy. ADAMTS13 activity decreases physiologically in second/third trimester. Recommendations: ADAMTS13 activity monitoring every 4 weeks during pregnancy; prophylactic FFP or caplacizumab if ADAMTS13 activity drops below 20%; close hematology-obstetrics co-management required.

output.summary: Published evidence documents TTP relapse rates of 17–25% in subsequent pregnancies. Literature reports physiological ADAMTS13 activity decrease during the second and third trimester in iTTP patients. Population-level data on ADAMTS13 monitoring protocols, prophylactic plasma infusion, and anti-vWF therapy during pregnancy summarized above.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Immune (acquired) thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) with thrombotic microangiopathy-mediated acute exacerbation of small-fiber neuropathy

differential.key_features: Pregnancy-associated; differentiate by ADAMTS13 activity (≥10% in HELLP, <10% in TTP), AST/ALT, and timing.
Renal predominant; ADAMTS13 normal; complement panel and genetic testing.
ANA + anti-dsDNA + low complement; secondary TTP overlap can occur.
Demyelinating NCS pattern would shift toward CIDP; here axonal small-fiber pattern + hematologic findings argue otherwise.
Prior baseline; the new acute exacerbation needs a new explanation (TMA).

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: Urgent CBC + peripheral smear (schistocytes), LDH, haptoglobin, indirect bilirubin, ADAMTS13 activity + inhibitor
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (schistocytes, ↑LDH, ↓haptoglobin), thrombocytopenia, and ADAMTS13 activity <10% with inhibitor confirms iTTP

optimal_actions.action: Skin biopsy for intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IENFD below 97.5% lower limit for age/sex confirms small-fiber neuropathy

optimal_actions.action: Autonomic function testing (QSART, deep-breathing HRV, Valsalva)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sudomotor and/or cardiovagal dysfunction supports small-fiber / autonomic involvement

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Recognize MAHA + thrombocytopenia + neurologic symptoms = thrombotic microangiopathy; obtain ADAMTS13 urgently
Initiate plasma exchange and immunosuppression (rituximab, corticosteroids) without waiting for ADAMTS13 if iTTP suspected (PLASMIC score)
Manage in coordination with hematology / maternal-fetal medicine
Address the small-fiber neuropathy component with IENFD and autonomic testing once stable
contraindicated_actions: Do not transfuse platelets (in TTP, platelet transfusion can worsen thrombosis)
Do not delay plasma exchange while waiting for ADAMTS13 result
Do not attribute acute exacerbation to idiopathic SFN — the hematologic picture demands TMA workup
key_reasoning_points: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia + thrombocytopenia + neurologic symptoms = TMA spectrum
ADAMTS13 activity <10% with inhibitor confirms acquired TTP (iTTP)
TTP can cause peripheral nerve ischemia and small-fiber damage
Pregnancy is a known precipitant of iTTP

red_herrings.data_point: Prior diagnosis of 'idiopathic small fiber neuropathy'
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor acute presentation as 'flare of prior SFN'
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The new acute deterioration with hematologic findings demands TMA workup; the prior label does not explain the systemic picture.
